subject.title: fix(doctor): flag missing plugin install paths

question: Should `openclaw doctor --fix` delete persisted plugin install records whenever the record's primary installPath/sourcePath no longer exists?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent and proven, but this is persisted user state repair semantics; automation cannot choose the desired compatibility policy for arbitrary missing plugin paths.

options.title: Accept missing-path cleanup
options.body: Merge after current-main refresh, treating a missing primary record path as stale registry state that doctor may remove.

options.title: Narrow the cleanup predicate
options.body: Ask for the repair to target only configured, official, or otherwise reinstallable plugins if arbitrary path records should not be deleted.

options.title: Pause for broader policy
options.body: Hold this PR if generic installed-plugin record deletion should be handled by a larger migration or plugin ownership policy.

recommendation.title: Accept missing-path cleanup
recommendation.body: Merge after current-main refresh, treating a missing primary record path as stale registry state that doctor may remove.

likelyOwner.reason: The key human choice is persisted installed-plugin index repair policy, and steipete has the strongest observed history on that storage surface.
